Just another $40B going into the "AI Infra" Bubble... 

Elon stated this $SPCX financing would primarily fund $NVDA GPU procurement H1 2027. Which indirectly increases demand for memory, networking, etc needed. 

In some other notes, VPEC today in UDN:  "InP substrates is seriously in short supply" in regards to suppliers like $AXTI. 

- Morgan Stanley believes that InP substrates, EML and CW lasers will be the primary bottlenecks

- VPEC emphasized that whoever can secure more raw material supply in the future will have greater pricing power and influence in the market. 

Very true about supply procurement... both upstream materials like epiwafers/substrates to ultimately compute.

We're in a volatile period where all your largest companies in the world are fighting over control of the future of AI infrastructure.

Any slowdown seems unlikely.

tweets.text:
Not actively. I've been pointing out issues with Neocloud/Colo financing since 2025 from $SLNH to $CRWV debt interest. 

And maintain my opinion only a few neoclouds would survive in a few years, given they build enough of a moat to differentiate themselves against hyperscalers. 

So I don't think Elon's comments are completely wrong about Neoclouds, but there's nuances. 

One example was $NBIS SOFR + 2.75% $3.5B facility with Citibank, which actually has better rates than GPU financing from $2T+ companies. 

So kinda hard to say neocloud financing has "entirely shut off" since this Citibank facility was announced 3D ago

I'm not arguing the merits of Elon's claims here. There's some truth to them, even if they're framed in extremes.

I'm happy to hear his opinion on the direction of the industry... but if they're mainly amplifying concerns about competitor downfall (which benefits $SPCX + $TSLA)

There's some cause for concern about how healthy that is to the town square dynamic Elon originally envisioned with X.

Not actively. I've been pointing out issues with Neocloud/Colo financing since 2025 from $SLNH to $CRWV debt interest. 

And maintain my opinion only a few neoclouds would survive in a few years, given they build enough of a moat to differentiate themselves against hyperscalers. 

So I don't think Elon's comments are completely wrong about Neoclouds, but there's nuances. 

One example was $NBIS SOFR + 2.75% $3.5B facility with Citibank, which actually has better rates than GPU financing from $2T+ companies. 

So kinda hard to say neocloud financing has "entirely shut off" since this Citibank facility was announced 3D ago

I'm not arguing the merits of Elon's claims here. There's some truth to them, even if they're framed in extremes.

I'm happy to hear his opinion on the direction of the industry... but if they're mainly amplifying concerns about competitor downfall (which benefits $SPCX + $TSLA)

couple answers:
- warehouse aims to stay ~1000 packs ahead of digital (i.e. 1000 packs in the queue at all times)
- they have inventory of boxes/cases as well as packs. Those only get opened when needed. Onchain nobody has boxes/cases yet. Redeem packs to create boxes, redeem boxes to create cases. This redemption fails if existing digital product already equals physical sealed product (i.e. if people have 100 cases onchain and the warehouse only has 100 sealed cases, somebody cannot create a new onchain case even if they have enough boxes to do so)

thread_tweets.text:
we = the program in this case, the randomization is onchain.

before a rip nobody publicly sees what's in a pack, only a sealed onchain commitment. Our 3PL knows contents because they pack them. On our side, pack data is stored encrypted and only fetched when a rip needs it.

the credentials to fetch from the warehouse are stored securely in aws secrets manager, yuga devops and myself have access. An upgrade there would be to have the 3PL only return pack contents once the pack has been assigned to a rip onchain, which is doable (might add ~1s latency to pack rips but seems a worthy tradeoff) but for now really only ~2-3 people on yuga side can fetch from the queue and any fetches are logged.

- neoclouds are incredibly disorganised and lack ability to deliver on their contracts. this will result in an implosion in 2027. 

- hyperscalers are losing money on billions of dollars worth of gpus collecting dust because they can’t power them. anthropic s-1 rumored to prove this (releasing tmr i think)

- there’s no more money in the debt market to lend to scalers. investment-grade loans require independent lines of revenue generation and 200+ neoclouds will fail this.

bonus: insurance market is scrambling to support $1-5M penalties charged by labs / hyperscalers to data center builders who’ve fallen behind on delivery times. 

2027 is going to be bumpy. period of up-only is over for a bit.
